chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I complain to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about my loneliness and my restlessness among the people of Medina, until you come and I see you and am comforted by you. If only this tyrant would permit me, I would take a fortress in al-Ta'if, dwell in it, and make you dwell with me. I would guarantee to him that no unpleasantness would come from our side to him ever.'

key_terms.الطَّاغِيَة: The tyrant (referring to the Abbasid caliph)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about his loneliness and his proposed residence in al-Ta'if?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates the spiritual and social isolation of the Imams during the period of political quietism, expressing a desire for a secure, secluded residence in al-Ta'if to live among their devoted followers. He offers a pragmatic political guarantee to the ruling Umayyad caliphate that their presence would not pose a threat, highlighting the strategic patience and diplomatic nuance of the Imams amidst the 'Tahkim' (subjugation) era. This reflects the broader Shia scholarly understanding of the Imams' dual role as spiritual guides and political figures navigating the constraints of Abbasid and Umayyad authority.

If only this tyrant would allow me, so I (a.s.) would take a fort in Al-Taef, so I (a.s.) would dwell in it and you would all dwell in it with me (a.s.).
